artists.biography: Justin Townes Earle (born January 4, 1982) is an American singer-songwriter and musician. Earle records with Bloodshot Records and has five released albums from 2007–2012. He is the son of alternative country artist, Steve Earle.  Earle grew up in South Nashville, Tennessee, with his mother, Carol Ann Hunter Earle. His father Steve Earle gave Justin his middle name in honor of his mentor Townes van Zandt, but left Justin's mother when he was 2.

Earle records with Bloodshot Records and has five released albums from 2007–2012. He is the son of alternative country artist, Steve Earle.  Earle grew up in South Nashville, Tennessee, with his mother, Carol Ann Hunter Earle. His father Steve Earle gave Justin his middle name in honor of his mentor Townes van Zandt, but left Justin's mother when he was 2.

perplexity.description:
Harlem River Blues," released on September 14, 2010, is the third studio album by Justin Townes Earle, issued through Bloodshot Records. The album blends elements of country, folk, rock, and Americana, showcasing Earle's storytelling prowess and his ability to merge traditional roots music with contemporary sensibilities. Its sound is characterized by acoustic guitar-driven arrangements, subtle electric guitar, organ, and upright bass, creating a warm, intimate atmosphere that complements the reflective and narrative lyrics.

Positioned after his 2009 album "Midnight at the Movies," "Harlem River Blues" further established Earle's reputation as a significant voice in modern Americana and country music. The album received critical acclaim, earning an aggregate Metacritic score of 83/100, with reviewers praising its songwriting, emotional depth, and cohesive production. Notable tracks like the title song "Harlem River Blues" and "Workin' for the MTA" highlight Earle's skill in blending personal storytelling with broader social themes, contributing to the album's strong standing in his discography and among fans of the genre.
